note: Each entry is one localised edit to one styxx.v8 module: `old` must occur exactly once, `new` replaces it, and the committed conformance set is replayed against the result. `control: true` marks a semantics-preserving edit; a control the set catches voids the run, because the set would then be detecting that a file was touched rather than that a behaviour changed. The catalogue deliberately includes places the set is expected to miss -- an append-time refusal has no entrypoint in the set, and a rounding rule only bites past the ninth decimal -- because a catalogue that avoids the thin places reports a higher rate and means less.

mutations.name: merkle-leaf-prefix-dropped
mutations.why: RFC 6962 hashes a leaf as SHA-256(0x00 || entry). Without the prefix a leaf and a bare entry hash alike, which is the second-preimage hole the prefix exists to close. Expected to be MISSED: section 10 makes leaf hashes an INPUT to the merkle family, so no vector ever calls merkle.leaf_hash and a port could get the leaf prefix wrong and pass the whole set.

mutations.name: merkle-node-prefix-is-leaf-prefix
mutations.why: An interior node hashed with the leaf prefix makes a node and a leaf indistinguishable to a verifier reading hashes alone.

mutations.name: merkle-empty-root-is-zeros
mutations.why: RFC 6962 fixes MTH([]) = SHA-256(""). Thirty-two zero bytes is the other plausible choice and a port could pick it.

mutations.name: merkle-children-swapped
mutations.old: return node_hash(_mth(leaves, lo, lo + k), _mth(leaves, lo + k, hi))
mutations.new: return node_hash(_mth(leaves, lo + k, hi), _mth(leaves, lo, lo + k))
mutations.why: The left subtree is the first k leaves. Swapping the children keeps every leaf in the tree and changes every root above two leaves.

mutations.name: keys-small-order-accepted
mutations.old:
if _is_small_order(point):
        raise ValueError("public key is a small-order point")
mutations.new:
if False:
        raise ValueError("public key is a small-order point")
mutations.why: A small-order issuer key makes a signature verify under keys the signer does not hold. MISSED, and the reason is the finding: the rule is implemented TWICE. keys.decode_public calls validate_public, and cert.public_key_reason then runs its own copy of _decode_point/_is_small_order over the same bytes. Break either copy and the other still rejects the key, with the same reason prefix, so no vector's outcome moves. Its cert-side twin below is missed for the mirror-image reason.

mutations.name: cert-small-order-key-accepted
mutations.why: The same rule, mutated in cert.py's own copy. MISSED for the mirror-image reason: keys.decode_public has already raised on the key by the time this line would run, and the raise lands in the same 'issuer.key: ' reason prefix, so the recorded reason KIND does not move. Neither copy can be broken alone in a way this set sees, and the expect shape -- reason kinds, not reason texts -- could not tell the two rejections apart even if it did.

mutations.name: cert-noncanonical-point-accepted
mutations.old:
if y >= _P:
        return "non-canonical point encoding (y >= p)"
mutations.new:
if False:
        return "non-canonical point encoding (y >= p)"
mutations.why: Two encodings of one point, both accepted, give one issuer two issuer.key strings and one cert two valid forms. MISSED, and the layering is again the reason: keys.decode_public's canonical-base64url check and _decode_point reject the same bytes first, under the same reason prefix.

mutations.name: keys-tag-separator-dropped
mutations.why: The NUL between the tag and the digest is what makes the tag unambiguous. Without it, a tag that is a prefix of another tag can be made to collide.

mutations.name: log-sth-tag-dropped
mutations.old: if not keys.verify(public, keys.tagged(STH_TAG, digest), signature):
mutations.why: An STH signature is over the tagged digest. Verifying the bare digest lets a signature made for another object type be presented as an STH.

mutations.name: log-inclusion-tree-size-unchecked
mutations.why: An inclusion proof is only meaningful against the tree size it was cut at; accepting a proof for another size accepts a proof against a root nobody signed.

mutations.name: log-duplicate-id-accepted
mutations.old: raise AppendRefused(f"duplicate: {cert_id} is already at index {self.find(cert_id)}")
mutations.why: Append refuses a cert already in the log. Expected to be MISSED: section 10 records no append entrypoint, so nothing in the set ever calls it. Carried because the miss is the finding.

mutations.name: cert-embedded-ids-unchecked
mutations.old:
if value not in ref_ids:
            reasons.append(f"refs: embedded id {value} at {path} is not in refs")
mutations.new:
if False:
            reasons.append(f"refs: embedded id {value} at {path} is not in refs")
mutations.why: Section 2.1: every sha256 id embedded in subject/recipe/body must appear in refs, so a reader can resolve everything the cert leans on. Dropping the check accepts a cert that names a dependency it never declares.

mutations.name: cert-signature-not-verified
mutations.old: elif not keys.verify(public, keys.tagged(CERT_TAG, digest), signature):
mutations.why: A cert whose signature is merely well-formed rather than valid. The loudest possible failure, carried to show the set can see the loud ones.

mutations.name: cert-version-rule-inverted
mutations.old: return theirs is not None and mine is not None and theirs <= mine
mutations.new: return theirs is not None and mine is not None and theirs >= mine
mutations.why: Section 2.5 accepts a cert whose schema version is at or below the verifier's. Inverting it accepts exactly the certs a verifier cannot read and rejects the ones it can.

mutations.name: distance-absent-fill-minus-ten
mutations.why: Appendix B fills a token absent from one side's top-k with -20. Any other constant produces a different topk distance and therefore a different floor.

mutations.name: distance-one-sided-position-free
mutations.why: A position present on one side only contributes 5 * 20 and is counted. Contributing zero makes a run that stopped early look identical to one that did not.

mutations.name: distance-seqlp-sum-not-mean
mutations.why: seqlp is the mean of the absolute deltas, not their sum. A sum makes the distance grow with battery size and makes floors from batteries of different sizes incomparable.

mutations.name: distance-jsd-unhalved
mutations.why: Jensen-Shannon divergence is the mean of the two KLs, not their sum. Doubling every resid distance doubles the floor with it, so the verdicts move only where a distance sits near a floor that did not move.

mutations.name: floor-compare-before-rounding
mutations.old: d = None if distance is None else _rounded(_finite("distance", distance))
mutations.new: d = None if distance is None else _finite("distance", distance)
mutations.why: Section 5.2 compares both sides after rounding to nine places. Comparing an unrounded distance to a rounded floor turns a difference in the tenth decimal into a verdict. Expected to be caught only if some vector sits inside that window.

mutations.name: floor-exceeds-is-drift
mutations.why: GATED S5-02 recommendation A: an exceedance with no confirmation run is exceeds_floor, and drift is reserved for a comparison that ran the confirmation step. Collapsing them is the reversal the gate anticipates, and a verifier that made it would report drift where the spec says it cannot.

mutations.name: floor-is-mean-not-max
mutations.why: Section 5 defines the floor as the maximum pairwise distance between same-subject runs. A mean floor sits below half the observed nuisance and calls ordinary nuisance drift.

mutations.name: floor-alpha-off-by-one
mutations.why: The single-comparison level is 1/(m+1) over m pairs: the new comparison is the (m+1)th. Dividing by m alone overstates the confidence of every single verdict the floor supports.

mutations.name: control-leaf-hash-local-rename
mutations.why: A local variable renamed. Every byte the function returns is unchanged.

mutations.name: control-seqlp-named-return
mutations.why: The same value returned through a name. No arithmetic changes.

mutations.name: control-floor-same-negated
mutations.why: The same condition written the other way. Both d and f are finite floats by the time this runs, so the two agree everywhere.

mutations.name: control-cert-comment
mutations.new: # 8. numbers (section 2.1: no NaN, no infinity, nothing past 2**53)
mutations.why: A comment lengthened. Nothing executable is touched.
